Wouldn't trade the art thing though, still thinking about those damn melting cones.

text:
honestly, I keep thinking about how AI-generated video is gonna change things. It's not that I think it's *bad* tech, but I feel like people are mentally skipping over all the weird ethical stuff. Like, we're already struggling to tell what's real online, and now anyone can generate a clip of something that never happened. I know the companies claim they'll watermark it, but that feels like wishful thinking when deepfakes already exist and nobody can agree on how to regulate them.

What’s really on my mind is how this stuff reshapes trust. I don't think we've mentally adjusted to a world where video evidence just isn't reliable anymore. Lawyers, journalists, historians—they're all gonna have to fundamentally rethink their workflows. And sure, maybe creators will use it for cool art or mockups, but I honestly believe the average person is gonna get confused and exhausted trying to parse what's real.

I guess I'm not sad about it, just… watchful. We’ll eventually figure out some norms, but I doubt it’ll be smooth. Anyway, that's my two cents.

I keep seeing ads for these apps where you basically chat with a bot that’s supposed to be your friend or therapist or whatever, and it just feels… hollow. Like, I tried one out of curiosity and the damn thing kept saying "I understand how you feel" in this way that made me want to throw my phone. It’s not understanding shit, it’s just rearranging words it stole from real conversations.

We’re all so desperate for connection but we’re settling for this fake, plastic substitute. It’s a fucking bummer. I remember when people would just call each other or meet up for a coffee and actually bitch about their day. Now everyone’s glued to a screen, pouring their heart out to an algorithm that doesn’t give a single damn.

The light was nice today, though—got out for a walk. No app can beat that. Just fresh air and quiet. Probably won’t stop people from diving headfirst into this crap, but hey, I’ll be outside.

Had a pretty chill weekend, honestly. Saturday morning I finally got around to cleaning out the garage—been putting that off for a while, but it felt good to just get it done. Found an old box of Magic cards from high school, which was a nice surprise. Spent the afternoon just kind of hanging out, grabbed some tacos from that spot downtown.

Sunday was a bit more low-key. My buddy called and asked if I wanted to help him move a couch, so I swung by for an hour. After that, I sat on the porch with a beer and read some of that *Three-Body Problem* book everyone keeps talking about. It’s dense, but interesting. Thinking about maybe hitting the flea market next weekend if the weather holds.

Overall, nothing wild. Just the usual stuff—work, chores, a little bit of nothing. No big plans, just kinda letting the weekend roll. Kinda nice to have a weekend where you don’t have to force anything, you know?

text: Honestly, I’m still not sold on this whole “AI agent” thing where your phone or laptop just books stuff for you without asking. Like, yeah, I get the convenience angle, but every time I try one of those features it just books the wrong time or picks some random restaurant I’d never go to. Then I spend twenty minutes undoing it. Maybe in a year or two they’ll actually work, but right now it feels like a solution looking for a problem. Most people I know just manually tap a few buttons—it’s faster and you don’t end up with a haircut appointment in another city. The companies pushing this stuff act like we’re all drowning in chores, but I’ve got enough control as it is. I’ll pass on letting a bot mess with my calendar. Same with those auto-generated summaries in every app—half the time they miss the point anyway. I’d rather just read the damn email. So yeah, cool tech, but I’m not jumping on that bandwagon until it stops making basic mistakes.
